planning_ik_backend.description: Optional generic planning accelerator. cuRobo performs batch IK, self/world collision screening, and blocked-transit MotionGen on the GPU; PyBullet remains the final exact physics verifier.

base_support_height_m.description: Height of the physical plinth under the robot. Its collision footprint is derived from the grounded robot base link AABB, and it participates in placement, swept-clearance, rollout contact, and rendering.

contact_sequence.description: Adjacent robot-contact stages with the same value form one uninterrupted grasp. The harness approaches once, preserves contact between stages, and retreats only after the final stage.

release_before_phase.description: Optional explicit release boundary. It is required when this contact triggers later mechanism motion or precedes a passive return, and may not be later than the earliest such moving phase. The harness retains the verified contact gate through preceding plan-owned holds, opens the gripper and ends contact-gated actuation, executes the solved retreat, holds briefly at the safe endpoint, and only then enters the named phase.

interaction.description: Invariant benchmark policy: physical_push for maintain_width controls; explicit_ideal_feasibility is the legacy schema name for verified contact-gated object-joint actuation used by open_then_close grasps. After sustained bilateral contact, the plan-authoritative object-joint target follows the measured fractional dense-sample index along the current IK path through the identical smoothstep used during planning. The verified fingers and their nearest common rigid palm parent stop responding only to the target link to avoid a redundant solver loop; the remaining arm and every non-target object link stay collision-authoritative. No runtime grasp constraint is created. Frictional force-closure tuning is outside this benchmark.

rotation_xyzw.description: Application-owned cached contact rotation. It is regenerated from the collision-surface normal, the link's principal tangent, and contact_roll_deg before validation and use; agent-supplied values are ignored.

contact_roll_deg.description: The only agent-selected orientation datum after visual review. The application owns the common roll-zero frame and permits exactly five robot-IK rolls. Although 0 and 180 have symmetric jaw geometry, they remain distinct Panda wrist branches.

contact_frame_source.description: Machine-emitted provenance proving that contact_pose_link.rotation_xyzw was not authored by the agent.

allowed_robot_contact_links.description: Application-owned for centered open_then_close grasps: all Panda finger contact links are inserted automatically. A physical_push may still nominate the one semantic tool surface.

precontact_offset_m.description: Non-negative distance from the grasp target farther into free space along contact-pose local +Z. Robot approach moves in local -Z.

grasp_depth_m.description: Application-selected signed adjustment around the centered Panda grasp baseline along contact local +Z. For centered open_then_close, the placement solver ignores agent-supplied depth and searches a fixed shallow-to-deep lattice; value 0 includes the robot-defined 0.015 m inward useful-finger inset and produces an effective -0.015 m pose. Dense acceptance requires bilateral target proximity and no forbidden collision, and rollout independently requires sustained opposed two-finger contact before manipulation. maintain_width/tool-offset stages retain direct signed offset semantics. This remains after approach and is not approach clearance; precontact_offset_m is the separate positive transient free-space distance.

robot_tool_contact_offset_eef_m.description: Optional vector in the robot end-effector link frame from the EEF origin to the actual robot tool surface that must coincide with contact_pose_link. Use for maintain_width physical pushes such as one selected fingertip; the harness subtracts the rotated vector when solving the EEF origin. Omit for centered parallel-jaw grasps.

mode.description: Application-owned from interaction: explicit_ideal_feasibility becomes open_then_close and physical_push becomes maintain_width.

approach_finger_opening_m.description: Per-finger joint position during transit and approach. For open_then_close the generic application sets it from the selected final grasp width plus 0.005 m total jaw-aperture clearance (0.0025 m per finger); for maintain_width it equals finger_opening_m.

close_s.description: Time used to interpolate from approach_finger_opening_m to finger_opening_m while the arm holds the first contact pose. Must be positive for open_then_close and zero for maintain_width.

settle_s.description: Time to hold the acquired contact before object manipulation begins.

release_s.description: Time used to reopen at the final contact pose before retreat. Must be positive for open_then_close and zero for maintain_width.

manipulation_sample_hold_s.description: Physical dwell for each of the 65 ordered object-path samples. Increase it to execute the same plan path more slowly without changing any object endpoint or replaying object motion.

approach_waypoints_link_m.description: Ordered via-points for the transit into the precontact pose, expressed in the contacted link frame. Use these to route the wrist around an intervening link instead of straight through it.

transit_waypoints_world.description: Ordered world-frame end-effector poses used only while transiting from the preceding released retreat endpoint (or home for the first stage) to this stage's approach. Use geometry-derived poses to route around obstacles moved by earlier plan stages; these poses are not replayed during this stage's retreat.

release_retreat_waypoints_world.description: Agent-planned end-effector poses executed after opening the fingers and before release_before_phase begins. They must place the whole robot outside the released mechanism's swept volume. The harness adds a fixed nonzero endpoint settle before the object phase is enabled.

minimum_release_swept_clearance_m.description: Measured minimum whole-robot separation from every object link while moving through release_retreat_waypoints_world and while the declared passive-return joints sweep to rest. Any strictly positive value passes; the application adds no hidden clearance threshold.

forbidden_contact_links.description: Application-owned enumeration of every object link except contact_link. Checked at planning time against the whole swept path; agent-supplied lists are ignored.

minimum_swept_clearance_m.description: Required separation from forbidden_contact_links along the approach and manipulation path.

control_execution.description: Exhaustive, auditable ownership of every plan timeline control. Ownership is per control rather than per phase because one phase may combine a passive return with a different internally actuated motion.

energy_source.description: Physical source that performs an internal-mechanism control after the robot trigger. Desired motion or a phase name is not an energy source.

justification.description: Required human-auditable reason for any internal mechanism; it must describe the trigger/transmission rather than merely restate the desired motion.

release.description: Second, later object-side phase reached when the measured driver returns toward rest. Models a plan phase such as a lid closing after a pedal is released; without it a latched effect could never return.

settle_s.description: Seconds the robot holds at home after the last stage. Must be long enough for any declared causal release to reach its plan endpoint.

ik.description: Bounded initial-contact IK search budget. Dense manipulation always follows the nearest local joint-space branch; pose tolerances and joint-step rejection are not task parameters.
